title: Cellular G-action on an abstract cell complex
body_html:
Cellular $G$-action on an abstract cell complex

Let $X$ be an [[abstract cell complex|node:abstract_cell_complex.abstract_cell_complex]] and let $G$ be a group acting on $X$. The action is cellular if it preserves the face relation and the dimension function:

  • for all $g \in G$ and $E \preceq F$ in $X$, $g \cdot E \preceq g \cdot F$;
  • for all $g \in G$ and $E \in X$, $\dim(g \cdot E) = \dim E$.

Equivalently, $G$ permutes the cells and preserves the entire graded face poset. This is the combinatorial content of "$G$ acts by cellular homeomorphisms" on the geometric realisation.

For a cell $E \in X$ there are two natural subgroups of $G$ attached to $E$:

  • the setwise stabiliser $$\Stab_G(E) := \{g \in G : g \cdot E = E\};$$
  • the pointwise fixator $$\Fix_G(E) := \bigcap_{F \preceq E} \Stab_G(F) \;=\; \{g \in G : g \cdot F = F \text{ for every } F \preceq E\}.$$

The pointwise fixator is the combinatorial shadow of "$g$ fixes $E$ and its entire boundary": $g \in \Fix_G(E)$ requires $g$ to fix not only $E$ itself but every face $F \preceq E$ (setwise, which at the poset level is the same as pointwise on a single cell of the discrete face poset). In particular $\Fix_G(E) \le \Stab_G(E)$, and the inclusion is strict as soon as $E$ has a proper face on which $G$ acts nontrivially. Equality $\Fix_G(E) = \Stab_G(E)$ holds automatically when $E$ is a minimal cell (a vertex), where there are no proper faces.

This distinction is already visible at the combinatorial level — it is not merely a topological artefact. The paper's pointwise/setwise convention thus transports without change: $\Fix_G(E)$ is always the subgroup fixing $E$ and its boundary; $\Stab_G(E)$ is the coarser "permutes $E$ to itself" subgroup. Downstream axioms such as $P_E \subseteq \Fix_G(E)$ (paper's (P3)) use the finer subgroup. See the design remark in Recovering the induction data from a quasi-fundamental domain for the QFD implications.

Downstream

The cellular-action structure is the standing hypothesis of the QFD and induction machinery: Quasi-fundamental domain, QFD orbit lemma: gE = hF iff there is n with nE=F and g⁻¹hn fixes E, [[node:equivariant_sheaves.induction_GxP_X]] all take it as input.

Lean formalization

class GCellComplex (G : Type*) [Group G] (X : Type*)
    [PartialOrder X] [AbstractCellComplex X] [MulAction G X] : Prop where
  smul_le  : ∀ (g : G) {E F : X}, E ≤ F → (g • E) ≤ (g • F)
  smul_dim : ∀ (g : G) (E : X),
    AbstractCellComplex.dim (g • E) = AbstractCellComplex.dim E

GCellComplex G X is a pure Prop compatibility class stacked on top of [MulAction G X] and [AbstractCellComplex X]. Bundling the group action into the class is deliberately avoided: the cell complex data (dimension, face relation) and the action are independent inputs.

The setwise stabiliser $\Stab_G(E)$ is Mathlib's MulAction.stabilizer G E : Subgroup G; membership is MulAction.mem_stabilizer_iff. It takes only [MulAction G X] and does not depend on the cell-complex structure. This is the natural stabiliser of a poset element under a poset-respecting group action.

The pointwise fixator $\Fix_G(E)$ is the infimum

def pointwiseFix (G : Type*) [Group G] {X : Type*}
    [PartialOrder X] [MulAction G X] (E : X) : Subgroup G :=
  ⨅ F ∈ {F : X | F ≤ E}, MulAction.stabilizer G F

which depends on the poset structure through the down-set $\{F : F \preceq E\}$. Both concepts are needed and neither replaces the other:

  • $\Stab_G(E)$ is what makes the $G$-action a well-defined map on poset elements — the natural symmetry of a single cell as an abstract object.
  • $\Fix_G(E)$ is the combinatorial trace of "fixes the closure of $E$" and shows up whenever a cosheaf-like family $\{P_E\}$ has to interact with cells below $E$.

The induction / QFD machinery in SheafOnBuilding.QuasiFundDomain and SheafOnBuilding.Induction is stated with MulAction.stabilizer G E — the setwise version — and that choice is deliberate: the abstract framework tracks the $G$-action on individual poset elements and the residual factorisation $g^{-1} h n \in \mathrm{Stab}_G(E)$ that comes out of the InductionRel calculation. The pointwise refinement re-enters when a specific geometric or subgroup-theoretic input (a cell fixator that is automatically down-monotone) is available; that is where the distinction from the paper's conventions surfaces.

class GCellComplex (G : Type*) [Group G] (X : Type*)
    [PartialOrder X] [AbstractCellComplex X] [MulAction G X] : Prop where
  /-- The action preserves the face relation. -/
  smul_le : ∀ (g : G) {E F : X}, E ≤ F → (g • E) ≤ (g • F)
  /-- The action preserves dimension (cells map homeomorphically). -/
  smul_dim : ∀ (g : G) (E : X),
    AbstractCellComplex.dim (g • E) = AbstractCellComplex.dim E
